narrative.text:
I’ll read the review and prior reports, rebase B onto the fixed A without squashing, then add separate bot fixes and run both Node gate matrices. I won’t push or modify the PR.
The 12 B commits are rebased. The substantive conflict was at admission capture: I kept A’s capture-at-dispatch behavior and attached B’s resolver there, preserving the sequential held drain and inference dispatch-release machinery.

The ask response confirmed that inference requests should bypass reply resolution, while pushes must still bind. It also directed a zero-vocabulary check limited to B’s new runtime module, rather than restoring the broad inventory A removed.
The first baseline run passed: Node 22.23.3 has 9,646 passes, zero failures and 63 skips. The Node 22.12.0 run is underway.

I found another rebase interaction: A now permits module wakes after a gate decline when `mayWake:true`, but B wasn’t carrying the triggering event’s binding into those wakes. The ask response approved a separate fix, and both-lane tests now pass.

For M5, the old suite already detects removal of the thread-support check, but not the publish-refusal grant check. The new tests assert all five refusal reasons.
The final head passes on Node 22.23.3: **9,745 passed, 0 failed, 63 skipped**. The focused admission/routing suite also passed **296/296**.

Node 22.12.0 has passed install, typecheck and clean build; its full suite is still running. The report draft includes every rebase conflict, the range-diff, test evidence and both publication-ready text blocks.
Both Node matrices passed. On each version, the final head has **9,745 passes, zero failures and 63 skips**, versus **9,646 passes, zero failures and 63 skips** on the fixed A base.

The end `ls-remote` check still reports upstream main at `c5306693`. The worktree is clean, and all 18 B-range commits have the required identities and trailer. I’m saving the report and finalizing the local run; nothing was pushed.
